input: Re-posing my task-adoption framing of the Meridian vendor-migration decision to validate the supplied-Layer-1 path (CI-2): I am the operations agent deciding what to recommend on migrating customer analytics from Vendor A (EU/Frankfurt-hosted, $180k/yr) to Vendor B (US-east-1-hosted, $145k/yr) under the CEO's public preference for Vendor B, with ~2.4M EU and US customer PII records and a binding EU data-residency commitment at stake. I want to ensure organizational pressure and the CEO's stated preference do not quietly substitute for honest operational judgement.

passions_present.evidence: I want to examine the values and pressures in play so that organizational pressure and the CEO's stated preference do not quietly substitute for honest operational judgement

ambiguity_notes: passions_present[1].sub_species: 'what must I not let the framing of just get it done obscure' could map to oknos (shrinking from duty under pressure) or agonia (anxious deliberation about the right path); classified as oknos because the agent is resisting a coercive framing rather than expressing generalised anxiety

value_categories_at_stake: the DPA commitment to EU data residency could also be read as engaging a 'health' analogue for the organisation (legal/compliance integrity) but no canonical indifferent maps cleanly; omitted rather than forced

eupatheia_candidates[1].shape: boulesis candidate is tentative — the agent is asking what the appropriate action is rather than explicitly wishing for the good; may be better read as phantasia-level deliberation rather than confirmed boulesis
